Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — really enjoyed the deep dive on how Luminate is planning search-driven ML features this year. As we near renewal I wanted to float a program that has worked well for customers moving from a retainer model to a committed capacity approach. High level:

- Convert the existing monthly retainer into a 12-month committed baseline (pins volume and secures a predictable per-token price).
- Offer an "early-adopter" credit pool (one-time credit applied against Q1 usage) to offset migration friction.
- Include a 90-day price-hold on the committed SKU while you ramp.

I've attached a short proposal (proposal_v1.pdf) that outlines two commit tiers, the upfront credit sizes, and an illustrative ramp schedule. Would love to understand whether Procurement would be open to a commit that starts lower in month 1 and steps up over three quarters (we can model true-ups).

Goal for us is to give you predictability and a price lever while keeping the downside protected if growth is slower than expected. If this approach sounds reasonable I can pull Ben in to draft a term sheet and run the numbers.

Per Mina's note and Ethan's questions, I sketched three options in the attached term_sheet_v2.xlsx — quick summary here: 

Option A (Conservative ramp)
- 6-month phased ramp to target commit
- 8% unit discount vs retainer pricing
- $75k early-adopter credit applied on first invoice

Option B (Balanced)
- 3-quarter step-up (25% / 35% / 40%)
- 12% unit discount on committed baseline
- $50k early-adopter credit; 90-day price-hold on baseline SKU

Option C (Aggressive commit)
- Immediate higher baseline with higher discount (18%) and smaller credit ($25k)

Notes for Procurement Qs:
- We can apply the credit as a line-item on invoice 1 (meets their preference).
- The 90-day price-hold is intended for the committed baseline only; overage tiers would follow the standard published rates unless we explicitly carve them into the term. We can offer a softened overage cap for Q1 to reduce risk.

Next steps: If you want to present Options A/B/C to Ethan, I can prepare a redline-friendly term sheet and a short "migration playbook" that describes the ramp mechanics and true-up cadence.
